pid_data.process_description: H2/N2 Gas Mixing and Receiver Tank System including customer-side N2 100% and H2 100% supply lines through intake filters and pressure regulators, H2 feed to Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex), mixed gas transfer to the 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank, receiver tank monitoring by H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration, normal outlet line from the receiver tank to the downstream Process through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1), and emergency N2 purge/flush line with emergency control and vent discharge to roof on SV (V-17,18,19) it end scope of node. This system receives N2 100% and H2 100% from the customer-side gas supply lines through intake filters and pressure regulators. The gases are regulated to approximately 8 bar before entering the A-IET scope. The H2 stream is routed through the Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex) and then sent to a 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank with a maximum pressure of 10 bar. The receiver tank stores and buffers the mixed hydrogen-containing gas before it is supplied to the downstream process at approximately 4.5-5 bar. The outlet gas passes through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1) before entering the process. An H2 analyzer with auto-calibration continuously monitors hydrogen concentration in the receiver tank and sends signals to the Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control system. Under abnormal hydrogen concentration or pressure conditions, the emergency logic can isolate the normal process outlet, open the N2 emergency line, and vent or flush gas to the roof through the vent line.

equipment.name: Nitrogen intake filter
equipment.context: Customer-scope N2 100% intake filter upstream of pressure regulation; visible note: intake filter <=50 micron. Nitrogen SDS metadata: product is 100% nitrogen, compressed gas, simple asphyxiant, SDS #001040, CAS 7727-37-9, UN1066, transport class 2.2, hazard H280 contains gas under pressure and may displace oxygen causing rapid suffocation.

equipment.name: Hydrogen intake filter
equipment.context: Customer-scope H2 100% intake filter upstream of pressure regulation; visible note: intake filter <=50 micron. Hydrogen SDS metadata: product is 100% hydrogen, compressed gas and flammable gas Category 1, SDS #001026, CAS 1333-74-0, UN1049, transport class 2.1, hazards H220 extremely flammable gas and H280 contains gas under pressure; may form explosive mixtures with air, burns with invisible flame; flammable limits 4% to 76%, auto-ignition temperature 500 to 571 degC.

equipment.name: Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex)
equipment.context: A-IET scope gas mixer shown in dashed package; receives regulated gas feed from customer-side H2/N2 supply lines and sends mixed hydrogen-containing gas toward the receiver tank. Ex-rated model name visible as MG 100-2ME(Ex). Nearby piping note: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent; visible local run lengths include L=6 m and L=10 m around mixer/receiver piping.

equipment.name: Receiver Tank
equipment.context: Vertical stainless-steel receiver tank; visible label: Receiver Tank, Stainless Steel, 500 L, Max. 10 Bar. Stores and buffers mixed hydrogen-containing gas before outlet to downstream process. Tank outlet is labelled outlet 4.5-5 bar with L=2 m line near outlet manifold.

equipment.name: Vent-line FA device
equipment.context: Inline device labelled FA on the receiver vent line to roof; located on vent/flush discharge path. Exact FA meaning is not fully legible on drawing; appears associated with protection/analyzer or vent protection service on the roof vent line.

equipment.name: Power Supply
equipment.context: Power Supply box shown feeding control/HMI/emergency control area. Electrical supply supports HMI Programming and Emergency Control functions; no electrical rating visible.

valves.context: N2 pressure regulator on customer-side N2 100% supply; visible notes indicate regulator 8 bar and regulator 3.5 bar in customer scope, with process description confirming gases regulated to approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope. Associated with intake filter <=50 micron.

valves.context: H2 pressure regulator on customer-side H2 100% supply; visible notes indicate regulator 8 bar and regulator 3.5 bar in customer scope, with process description confirming gases regulated to approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope. valves.context: Untagged red valve symbol inferred as solenoid/isolation valve on regulated N2 feed assembly. Associated with customer-side N2 feed and emergency N2 service. Exact tag, size, fail position, and normal position are not visible.

valves.context: Untagged red valve symbol inferred as check/backflow prevention valve on N2 feed. Nitrogen SDS advises use of a backflow preventative device in the piping. Exact tag, size, rating, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Hydrogen regulated feed assembly upstream of MG-100-2ME(Ex)
valves.context: Untagged red valve symbol inferred as solenoid/isolation valve on regulated H2 feed to gas mixer. Hydrogen service is extremely flammable compressed gas. Exact tag, size, fail position, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Hydrogen regulated feed assembly upstream of MG-100-2ME(Ex)
valves.context: Untagged red valve symbol inferred as check/backflow prevention valve on H2 feed to gas mixer. Hydrogen SDS advises use of a backflow preventative device in piping. Exact tag, size, rating, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Mixed gas line between MG-100-2ME(Ex) and TK-500L
valves.context: Valve shown as SV (27) on mixer outlet/receiver inlet line. Customized programming note: during 9% H2 emergency sequence valve 27.5/27 remains open initially; if H2 concentration is not reduced below 9% after 10 min, valve 27 is closed and an alarm is given; mixer is stopped.

Manual valve symbol labelled MV on vertical manifold adjacent to receiver tank outlet and vent path. Used for local isolation/operation of receiver outlet/vent manifold. Exact size, rating, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Normal receiver outlet line to downstream Process
valves.context: Valve shown as SV (21.1) on normal outlet line downstream of TK-500L. Customized programming note: in the case of 9% H2, valve 21.1 will be closed to isolate the normal process outlet. Outlet service is mixed gas at approximately 4.5-5 bar.

valves.location: Normal receiver outlet line downstream of SV-21.1 before Process boundary
valves.context: Valve shown as CV (12.1) on normal outlet line to downstream Process. Associated with mixed gas receiver outlet at approximately 4.5-5 bar. Exact valve size, rating, fail position, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Receiver tank vent/flush line to roof
valves.context: Valve shown as SV (21.2) on vent line to roof. Customized programming note: in the case of 9% H2, valve 21.2 opens and the wrong gas will be flushed over roof; customer can decide if valve 21.2 is left open to empty the receiver.

valves.location: Receiver tank vent/flush line to roof near FA-1
valves.context: Valve shown as CV (12.2) on vent/flush path to roof. Associated with emergency vent discharge from receiver tank. Exact valve size, rating, and normal position are not visible.

valves.location: Emergency N2 line into receiver outlet/purge header
valves.context: Valve shown as SV (21.3) on the N2 emergency line. Customized programming note: in the case of 9% H2, valve 21.3 opens the N2 emergency line for purge/flush service.

valves.location: Emergency N2 line downstream of SV-21.3
valves.context: Valve shown as CV (12.3) on the N2 emergency line, downstream of SV-21.3. Provides check/backflow prevention on nitrogen emergency purge/flush line. Exact size, rating, and normal position are not visible.

instruments.function: Hydrogen concentration analyzer with auto-calibration; continuously monitors H2 concentration in receiver tank and initiates emergency logic on high H2 concentration.
instruments.location: Analyzer cabinet adjacent to TK-500L receiver tank
instruments.context: Visible label: H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration. Customized programming note: analyzer continuously controls the value of H2 gas in the receiver; in the case of 9% H2, emergency procedure is activated. Signal wiring shown to Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control. Cable length visible as 15 m to Control & Display; RS485 signal wiring distance approx. 300 m shown.

instruments.function: Control and display interface receiving analyzer/control signals.
instruments.location: Control & Display box above H2 Analyzer
instruments.context: Visible label: Control & Display. Connected by signal wiring from H2 Analyzer; visible cable length 15 m. Provides control/display interface for receiver H2 monitoring and emergency sequence indications.

instruments.function: HMI programming interface for monitoring and control logic.
instruments.location: HMI Programming box near Emergency Control
instruments.context: Visible label: HMI Programming. Connected by RS485/signal wiring with visible distance approx. 300 m. Receives/coordinates signals from analyzer/control system for emergency operation.

instruments.function: Emergency control logic for solenoid valve actions and alarm response.
instruments.location: Emergency Control panel near HMI Programming and emergency line valves
instruments.context: Visible label: Emergency Control. Customized programming: at 9% H2, close SV-21.1, open SV-21.3 N2 emergency line, keep/open SV-27 initially, open SV-21.2 to flush gas over roof, attempt return below 9% H2 for 10 min, then close SV-27 and alarm if not recovered; mixer stopped and problem investigated.

instruments.context: Red circular local instrument symbol appears on N2 feed/regulator assembly. Exact tag is not legible. Associated service: N2 100% compressed gas regulated to approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope.

instruments.context: Red circular local instrument symbol appears on H2 feed/regulator assembly. Exact tag is not legible. Associated service: H2 100% compressed gas regulated to approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope.

instruments.function: Local pressure indication on receiver outlet/emergency control header.

Emergency line piping note: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent. Nitrogen SDS metadata: compressed gas, simple asphyxiant, may displace oxygen and cause rapid suffocation, UN1066 class 2.2.

utility_lines.flow_direction: From customer-side H2 100% supply through intake filter/regulation into A-IET scope and toward MG-100-2ME(Ex) gas mixer.
utility_lines.context: H2 service visible as H2 (100%). Intake filter <=50 micron; regulator approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope. Piping note: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent. Hydrogen SDS metadata: extremely flammable compressed gas, may form explosive mixtures with air, burns with invisible flame, UN1049 class 2.1, flammable limits 4%-76%, auto-ignition 500-571 degC.

utility_lines.flow_direction: Into power supply/control system for HMI Programming and Emergency Control.

connections.context: Customer-side N2 100% supply to nitrogen intake filter. Scope start is customer-side N2 100% supply upstream of intake filter and pressure regulator. Visible note: intake filter <=50 micron. Nitrogen SDS: 100% nitrogen compressed gas, simple asphyxiant, H280, may displace oxygen causing rapid suffocation, UN1066 class 2.2.

Regulated N2 feed from intake filter through customer-scope regulator and inferred isolation/check valves toward A-IET gas mixing system. Process description states gases are regulated to approximately 8 bar before entering A-IET scope; drawing note also shows regulator 3.5 bar in customer scope. Piping note visible: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent. Flow direction follows feed arrows from N2 supply toward mixer/system.

Customer-side H2 100% supply to hydrogen intake filter. Scope start is customer-side H2 100% supply upstream of intake filter and pressure regulator. Visible note: intake filter <=50 micron. Hydrogen SDS: 100% hydrogen compressed flammable gas, H220 extremely flammable gas, H280 contains gas under pressure, may form explosive mixtures with air, burns with invisible flame, UN1049 class 2.1.

Regulated H2 feed from intake filter through customer-scope regulator and inferred isolation/check valves to Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex). Process description states regulated pressure approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope. Visible piping note: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent; local run near mixer labelled L=6 m. Flow direction follows feed arrow from H2 supply toward mixer.

Mixed hydrogen-containing gas transfer from Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex) to 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank through SV (27). Visible piping metadata includes 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent and local run length L=10 m near receiver/mixer package. Receiver data: stainless steel, 500 L, max 10 bar. H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration monitors receiver H2 concentration and sends signal wiring to Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control. Emergency programming: if H2 reaches 9%, SV-27 remains open initially, but after 10 min without recovery below 9% H2, SV-27 is closed, alarm given, and mixer stopped.

connections.to_id: Mixed H2/N2 gas to downstream Process
connections.context: Normal receiver outlet line from 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank to downstream Process through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1). Drawing label: outlet 4.5-5 bar; visible line length L=2 m near receiver outlet; outlet branch to Process shown with line note 1 inch x 2 inch. Process end is downstream process connection after SV (21.1) and CV (12.1). H2 analyzer/emergency control logic acts on this flow path: at 9% H2, SV-21.1 closes to isolate normal process outlet.

Receiver tank emergency vent/flush line from TK-500L outlet/vent manifold toward inline FA device and roof vent. Visible labels: To Roof (L=5 m), CV (12.2), SV (21.2), MV, and FA. Emergency programming: at 9% H2, SV-21.2 opens and wrong gas is flushed over roof; customer may decide to leave SV-21.2 open to empty receiver. Exact FA device details and valve sizes/ratings are not visible.

Final emergency vent/flush discharge from inline FA device to roof. Drawing label: To Roof (L=5 m). Service is receiver vent/flush gas during abnormal H2 concentration or purge operation. Emergency sequence opens SV-21.2 upstream so gas is discharged to roof; no downstream valve tag is visible on this segment.

Emergency N2 purge/flush line from filtered/regulator N2 supply into the receiver outlet/purge header associated with TK-500L. Visible label: Emergency Line. Valves shown on emergency branch: SV (21.3) and CV (12.3). Process description: under abnormal hydrogen concentration or pressure conditions, emergency logic opens the N2 emergency line and vents/flushes gas to roof. Customized programming: at 9% H2, SV-21.3 opens the N2 emergency line. Piping note: 1 inch S316L schedule 10 or equivalent; N2 regulator approximately 8 bar before A-IET scope.

Electrical power supply connection into the shown Power Supply box for controls. The drawing shows a Power Supply near HMI Programming and Emergency Control; no voltage, rating, cable size, or breaker information is visible.
